issues.failure_explanation: The allowed patches may meet the Dirichlet boundary, so a gradient minimizer cannot generally be shifted by a constant on K to prescribe its mean. For a concrete example, let connected K meet that boundary and let u_k^epsilon be a positive smooth bubble inside one mesh element contained in K. Its gradient is orthogonal to every elementwise-constant finite-element gradient. Every gradient minimizer therefore has zero gradient on K and, by the boundary condition, is zero there, so none has the bubble's positive mean.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use an unconstrained approximant and retain both its gradient error and d^{-1} times its L² error in the infimum. A gradient-only version instead needs a separately justified interior or boundary normalization.
issues.overall_effect: The construction used to obtain the gradient-only best-approximation term is invalid for boundary-touching patches covered by the setup.
